name: Reasoning and Proof
strandNote: Not needed to be hired. Research roles that hire maths PhDs, and reading proofs in papers.
description: Learn the logic behind every proof, then write proofs a stranger can check.

lessonNames.l1-true-or-false: Statements that are true or false
lessonNames.l8-functions-as-sets: A function as a set of pairs
lessonNames.l15-proof-a-stranger-can-check: A proof a stranger can check

lessonObjectives.l1-true-or-false: Tell a statement from a question or an opinion, and decide whether it is true.
lessonObjectives.l2-and-or-not: Build compound statements with and, or and not, and check them with a truth table.
lessonObjectives.l3-if-then: Read an implication, its converse and its contrapositive, and tell which ones say the same thing.
lessonObjectives.l4-for-all-there-exists: Write statements with “for all” and “there exists”, and see why their order matters.
lessonObjectives.l5-saying-the-opposite: Negate a statement with quantifiers and implications without changing its meaning by accident.
lessonObjectives.l6-sets: Describe a set by listing it and by a rule, and use membership and subsets.
lessonObjectives.l7-combining-sets: Combine sets with union, intersection, difference and complement, and prove De Morgan’s laws.
lessonObjectives.l8-functions-as-sets: Treat a function as a set of input and output pairs with a domain and a codomain.
lessonObjectives.l9-one-to-one-onto: Prove that a function is one-to-one or onto, and build its inverse when it is both.
lessonObjectives.l10-direct-proof: Prove a statement straight from definitions, such as “the sum of two even numbers is even”.
lessonObjectives.l11-contrapositive: Prove an implication through its contrapositive, such as “if $n^2$ is even then $n$ is even”.
lessonObjectives.l12-contradiction: Prove a statement by contradiction, including that $\sqrt{2}$ is irrational.
lessonObjectives.l13-induction: Prove a statement for every whole number by induction, including a sum formula.
lessonObjectives.l14-counterexamples: Disprove a general claim with a single counterexample, and tell when an example proves nothing.
lessonObjectives.l15-proof-a-stranger-can-check: Write a proof another reader can check line by line, with every step justified.
